newsitem.title: FRANCE: Flour firms want EU help to continue exports.
newsitem.headline: Flour firms want EU help to continue exports.

text.p: The head of France's largest flour milling firm, preparing for talks with the European Commission this month over recent cuts in export subsidies, said on Friday the industry would need licences to sell 450,000 tonnes of flour up to the end of June.

Michel Soufflet, president of Groupe Soufflet and a leading spokesman for the milling industry, said flour firms would also ask the European Union to create what amounted to a separate refund covering exports in the month of July.
The EU licence season ends on June 30, while intervention stocks are low and a new wheat crop will not arrive before late July.

"Since there are no intervention stocks, there has to be a restitution that would be valid essentially for July, with negative correctives (one-off monthly adjustments) before and afterwards," Soufflet said in an interview.

He said a meeting had been called at the European Commission for the middle of April to discuss the industry's requests, which follow a drop in flour export subsidies to below the level offered to help exporters ship the raw ingredient wheat.
Uppermost in millers' minds would be the need to increase flour refunds to viable levels and to agree on the quantities they would need to export, both before and during July, he said.
"We are going to say we need restitutions and to talk about the tonnage we need to go up to the end of June," he said, adding this figure was estimated at 450,000 tonnes.
"We are also going to talk about the tonnage in July, for which we need restitutions based on old-crop wheat."
The European Union on Thursday cut its main wheat flour refund, which has been as high as 27 Ecus this crop year, to five Ecus per tonne from eight Ecus and below the 7.49 given for wheat.
Soufflet said wheat aid had been driven down by a lack of licences in that market, but this had little to do with flour. Millers wanted a 37 percent premium for flour refunds restored.
